Traffic chaos in Perthshire villages after Google Maps glitch

2026-09-22 BBC Scotland (Claire Thomson, Sarah Farron) Google Maps, glitch, traffic diversion, Perthshire, A9, Dunkeld, Pitlochry, single-track road, navigation error
Read the source article

Quick summary

A Google Maps glitch falsely reported the A9 trunk road as closed and diverted drivers — including campervans and a coach — onto a narrow single-track road between Dunkeld and Pitlochry, trapping residents and causing chaos in Perthshire villages for three days.

Key takeaways

  • Google Maps falsely reported the A9 as closed, redirecting traffic onto the unclassified U163 road through Ballinluig, Tulliemet and Guay
  • The glitch began on Friday and persisted through the weekend; residents were unable to leave their homes due to excessive traffic on a road with no passing places
  • Campervans, a large coach, and cars with trailers (one towing a boat) were sent down the single-track road, some at speeds up to 40 mph
  • Transport Scotland publicly posted on X that Google Maps was falsely reporting the A9 as closed and recommending an "inconvenient alternate route"
  • The bug was fixed after the A9 Dual Action campaign group contacted the Google Maps team in London directly
  • Laura Hansler of the campaign group noted Google Maps had previously shown incorrect speed limits on the same trunk road
